questions.q: How are modes bound to switches?
options: To an AUX channel and a range
Through the OSD menu by switch name
questions.explain: A mode is active when the value of the AUX channel falls within the set range.

questions.q: Why must ARM be on a separate switch with no neighbors?
options: So that you do not arm by accident
The firmware requires it for the ARM mode
questions.explain: Several modes on one channel are an extra chance to arm at the wrong moment.

questions.q: Why keep ANGLE on a switch if you fly ACRO?
options: A rescue and a condition of AUTO-LAND
For the OSD elements with a horizon
questions.explain: Self-leveling brings the horizon back and is needed by the failsafe landing.

questions.q: When should FLIP OVER AFTER CRASH be turned on?
options: Only when the props are free
On the bench with props, as a check
questions.explain: The mode spins the motors in reverse — with snagged props that means a broken motor.

questions.q: Which voltage should the OSD show?
questions.explain: The average per cell reads the same on 4S and 6S and tells you the state of the battery right away.

questions.q: The low-voltage warning comes too late. Why?
options: High motor KV lowers the reading
questions.explain: Under load the voltage is lower — the threshold is set with a margin for the sag.

questions.q: Logic = 1 (AND) in the aux command means:
options: The mode on two channels at once
All AND rules of the mode are required
questions.explain: This is how two-switch combinations are made.

questions.q: Why leave a margin between the ranges of a three-position switch?
options: The CRSF protocol requires it for AUX
So that jitter does not toggle modes
